opportunities.title: CUSG SOAC: Operational funding
opportunities.amount: Part of per-year SOAC cap (about $1,000 new / $5,000 established)
opportunities.reasons: The club is a registered student organization and open to all students, and SOAC operational funding covers regular operating costs like meeting food and equipment. The Oct. 14 priority deadline has passed, but late requests are accepted with no guaranteed hearing slot, and the last Fall hearing is Nov. 18, so submit on BuffConnect right away after meeting your CSI liaison. If you miss it, the next hearing is Jan. 13.

opportunities.title: CUSG SOAC: Event funding
opportunities.amount: Part of per-year SOAC cap (about $1,000 new / $5,000 established)
opportunities.reasons: The club is an RSO open to all students, so it can ask SOAC for event and operations money, which could cover speaker events and meeting food. The priority deadline (Oct 14) has passed, but late requests are accepted with no guaranteed hearing slot, and the last fall hearing is Nov 18. Meet your CSI liaison and submit on BuffConnect right away. Hardware and AI tools may be harder to justify, and they must be stored on campus.
eligibility_flags: Must be open to all CU students
Priority deadline passed; late requests not guaranteed a hearing

opportunities.title: CUSG SOAC: Travel funding
opportunities.reasons: The club is a registered, open-to-all CU Boulder student organization, so it can apply to SOAC. Travel funding only helps if members go on an overnight trip, but SOAC's operations funding fits the goals of food and tools, and its events funding could cover speaker events. The priority deadline (Oct 14) has passed, so submit on BuffConnect right away to try for the last fall hearing on Nov 18, with no guaranteed slot. First meet with your CSI liaison. The next travel application deadline is Jan 4 for March travel.
eligibility_flags: Must be open to all students
Priority deadline passed; hearing slot not guaranteed
Student fees can't pay for food while traveling

opportunities.title: Arts & Sciences Student Government (ASSG) funding
opportunities.reasons: The club is a registered student organization and could request up to $1,000 per semester through a funding hearing. The page also requires the club to be affiliated with the College of Arts & Sciences, and we couldn't confirm that. Check with the Center for Student Involvement before putting in the effort. Food and AI tools may or may not be covered by the Student Fee Regulations.

opportunities.title: Gloo AI Hackathon
opportunities.reasons: This is a news article about the 2026 Gloo hackathon, which already happened (Oct 6-8, 2026). It was held in Boulder and had a $100,000 grand prize. The page doesn't give dates, rules or eligibility for a next edition, so I couldn't confirm the club could enter. It's a prize for a winning project, not funding for club food or tools, so watch for the next edition's official page.

opportunities.title: YC AI Student Starter Pack (credits via YC university events)
opportunities.amount: $25,000+ in credits per individual student (per the guide)
opportunities.reasons: This is a blog guide, not a club grant. Credits go to individual students who attend a YC university event in person, and the page doesn't say whether one is coming to CU Boulder. It's worth sharing with members as a free perk, but the club can't apply for money.
eligibility_flags: Must attend YC event in person

opportunities.title: Rocky Mountain AI Interest Group (RMAIIG)
opportunities.reasons: This is a community AI group, not a funding program, and the page lists no grants or application. It does hold events at CU Boulder (an AI Robotics Showcase on Nov 17 with a pizza sponsor), so it could be worth contacting about co-hosting or sponsor introductions.

opportunities.title: Engineering Excellence Fund (EEF)
opportunities.provider: CU Boulder College of Engineering and Applied Science
opportunities.reasons: The fund supports engineering education in the College of Engineering and Applied Science and reads proposals from engineering students and faculty. The page doesn't say whether a non-engineering club like AI Club can apply, and it gives no amounts or deadlines. It's worth emailing eef@colorado.edu to ask, especially about research hardware, but food and AI tools likely don't fit.

opportunities.title: AI for Altruism Grant Programs (incl. Student Engagement Funding)
opportunities.reasons: The page is a general list of AI education grants, and I couldn't find any "AI for Altruism" student engagement program on it. The grants it lists are large NSF and faculty-focused programs, which a student club can't realistically apply for.

opportunities.title: NSF FINDERS FOUNDRY
opportunities.reasons: Only nonprofits, governments, universities (applying for their faculty) and tribal nations can submit, so a student club can't apply directly. The program also funds K-12 AI education research teams, not club food, AI tools or hardware.

opportunities.title: IUSE / Professional Formation of Engineers: RED
opportunities.reasons: This NSF grant is for engineering department change projects. The lead applicant must be a Department Chair/Head, or a Dean or Provost, so a student club can't apply. It also doesn't cover food, AI tools or hardware.
eligibility_flags: Not a fit for club funding goals

# AI Club: SOAC Operational Funding Request

## Organization overview
AI Club is a registered student organization at CU Boulder, open to all students, founded about two years ago. We bring in speakers to teach CU students and faculty about evolving technology, especially AI. About 100 people attend our meetings, and our email list has 800+ people. We have 100 members. Our officers describe us as the biggest club at CU. We have also landed engagements with G2 and Techstars.

## How this supports our mission
Operational funding covers regular costs of carrying out our mission. Our speaker events and regular meetings are how we teach students and faculty about AI. The items below support that work.

## Requested items
1. **Food at meetings.** About 100 attendees per meeting. Cost per meeting: [[MISSING: food cost per meeting and number of meetings this semester]]
2. **AI tools for students.** [[MISSING: which tools, number of licenses, cost, how they will be distributed to students]]
3. **Hardware for research time.** [[MISSING: specific hardware, cost, vendor quote]]. Hardware will be [[ASSUMED: stored on campus and used for organizational, not personal, purposes, as SOAC requires]].

## Total request
[[MISSING: total amount requested]]. Awards count toward the per-year SOAC cap (about $1,000 for new organizations, about $5,000 for established ones). [[MISSING: whether SOAC treats AI Club as new or established]]

## Timeline and spending
We will meet with CSI Finance before spending approved funds and spend them by the deadline in the approval email (no later than May 1). [[MISSING: planned meeting dates and speaker event dates]]

## Contact
[[MISSING: officer name, email, and CSI liaison name]]

## Requirements checklist
- [ ] Must be an RSO open to all CU Boulder students
- [ ] Meet with assigned CSI liaison before submitting
- [ ] Submit the request on BuffConnect
- [ ] Oct. 14 priority deadline has passed; late requests are accepted but a hearing time is not guaranteed
- [ ] Last Fall 2026 SOAC hearing is Nov. 18; next is Jan. 13 (dates subject to change)
- [ ] Prepare for a SOAC funding hearing
- [ ] Hold a pre-spending meeting with CSI Finance after approval
- [ ] Spend operational funds by May 1; food funds must be spent by the date in the approval email
- [ ] Resources must be for organizational use and stored on campus where possible
- [ ] Follow the SOAC Code
assumptions: Hardware will be stored on campus and used for organizational purposes, as SOAC requires.

Our industry ties include AI, software, G2 and Techstars, and both G2 and Techstars have done engagements with the club.

Speaker events educate a broader CU audience about AI. [[MISSING: planned speakers, dates, expected attendance, and costs]]
